1:12 I took 3 years of American Sign Language and one of the first lessons they tell you is to never look at the interpreter. Deaf people already face a lot of exclusion, it can feel really dehumanizing if people won’t even look at you when they are speaking to you.

Also, interpreters are specifically trained to be a deaf persons voice. it is supposed to be like they aren’t even there at all, it is what they are paid to do. An interpreter is a means to communicate, not an advocate or caretaker or that kind of thing. It’s the same as if you were texting your friend, you would be addressing them, not the phone, because although you are using the phone to communicate, that is not who you are actually communicating with.
